title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks closed roughly flat Thursday after paring an early selloff - S&P 500 ended slightly lower, Nasdaq inched up, Dow fell 161 pts (-0.3%) - as hopes rose for a 'phased deal' reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Markets: Treasury yields hit fresh multi-decade highs - the 10-year climbed to ~5.20%, the 30-year to 5.46% (highest since the 2000s), and the 2-year neared 4.9%, its highest since May 2024; a Treasury long-bond buyback also fell short of expectations.

Markets: Bond volatility (MOVE index) spiked to levels last seen during the Iran war; Brent crude jumped ~3.4% to $106-107/bbl and WTI to ~$94.61 after Saudi Arabia intercepted Houthi missiles, raising fears of Red Sea supply disruption.
Companies: MGM Resorts plunged ~11% after Barry Diller withdrew his bid to buy the rest of the casino company he didn't already own.

Companies: Cracker Barrel (+4.5%) and General Mills (+1%) beat quarterly earnings estimates; IonQ rose 4.4% on a quantum error-decoder milestone; activist Starboard Value is pushing Knife River to explore a sale.
Macro/Policy: A Trump-Xi summit opened at the White House, with Trump touting 'tremendous strides' ahead of talks on trade, security and technology.
Macro/Policy: US and Iranian negotiators are reportedly discussing a phased deal in which Tehran allows Hormuz navigation in exchange for the US ending its naval blockade.

Macro/Policy: The Fed's Sept. 16 hike to 3.75%-4.00% (first in 3+ years) continues to reverberate, with markets pricing higher-for-longer rates; Friday brings final Michigan consumer sentiment, durable goods data, and remarks from Fed's Hammack and Williams.
